Lower Bounds The sample complexity bounds we prove in Theorem 1, 3, and 5 are optimal (up to log factors) in terms of the dependence on d, n, and log(1/δ). However, the question remains of resolving the optimal dependence on the bag size k. For every function class F, we have the trivial lower bound on the minimax sample  complexity of n = Ω(d log(1/δ)/(kε)) for the realizable setting and n = Ω d log(1/δ)/(kε2 ) for the agnostic setting, since LLP with n bags is only harder than supervised learning with nk examples. In general, the 1/k dependence in the lower bound cannot be improved, as there are function classes for which it is tight. For example, consider the function class F = {f0 , f1 } where fi (x) = i for i ∈ {0, 1}. For this class F, observing the label proportion α allows us to compute the average instance-level classification loss over the bag for both f0 and f1 . Therefore, LLP with n bags is no harder than supervised learning with nk labeled examples, so F can be PAC learned with O(1/(kε)) e samples 2 in the realizable setting and O(1/(kε )) in the agnostic setting. e
